slot.brief: Two blocks connected by a string over a pulley (or stacked with friction between them); draw free-body equations and solve the acceleration and tension.

stem: Two masses of $2\ \text{kg}$ and $6\ \text{kg}$ are connected by a light inextensible string over a frictionless pulley. Find the acceleration magnitude and string tension. Take $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.

verdicts.working: For an Atwood machine, a = ((6 - 2)/(6 + 2)) × 10 = 5 m s^-2. The tension is T = 2(10 + 5) = 30 N.

working:
$a=\dfrac{(6-2)g}{6+2}=5\ \text{m s}^{-2}$
$T=2(g+a)=30\ \text{N}$

Independent check: For an Atwood machine, a = ((6 - 2)/(6 + 2)) × 10 = 5 m s^-2. The tension is T = 2(10 + 5) = 30 N.
solution:
For an Atwood machine, $a=\dfrac{(m_2-m_1)g}{m_1+m_2}$.
$$a=\dfrac{(6-2)10}{6+2}=5\ \text{m s}^{-2}$$
For the $2\ \text{kg}$ mass, $T=m_1(g+a)=2(10+5)=30\ \text{N}$.
